instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Warmth with a Countdown
cards.instruction: Perform increasing warmth with increasingly final language, as though every act of care might also be a goodbye.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit in the good chair. I've put your favourite cup out; you should have the best of this place while you're here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm here every Thursday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And I'll pack the cup for you today. You can keep a little of our Thursdays wherever you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather leave it here and have another cup next week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave it here, then. I'll keep your chair free, for as many Thursdays as we have left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll pack your food. Take two sandwiches; I want you fed properly after you leave us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm going to the next town for the afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then take the flask too. You can have our tea even when you're not at our table.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can't carry all that. I only brought a small bag.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One sandwich, then. I'll cut it the way you liked as a child, so you leave with something familiar.

cards.title: Everything Has Two Prices
cards.instruction: Price every offer twice: once in practical terms and again through an emotional cost that grows when the offer returns.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll drive you to the station. You cover petrol and tell me why you stopped calling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cover petrol. I'm not doing the other part in a car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All right, we can drive quietly. Name a day for the conversation before I start the engine.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow. But you'll have to call me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Petrol today, then. Tomorrow you call first; I need to know you want the conversation as much as the lift.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll lend you the dress for ten pounds and an apology for calling it hideous.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Here's twenty. Can I just take it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the extra ten. I'll help with the zip once you tell me what changed your mind.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, it's beautiful. Can I wear it to the party now?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For ten, yes. And when they ask, tell them I chose it; don't say you rescued it from my wardrobe.

cards.title: Agree to the Exact Words
cards.instruction: Agree to the exact wording, then use later callbacks to narrow what those words can obligate you to do.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll organise this load. I agreed to carry one box to the van.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You promised to help me move.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: With one box. You choose it and I'll take it out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The biggest one, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Fine. Lift it into my arms. I agreed to carry it; you can handle getting it off the floor.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll have the dog fed and ready at eleven. I agreed to watch him today.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My train gets in at a quarter to midnight. Can't I collect him in the morning?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll bring him to the station, then. Meet me before the clock changes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You said you loved him. Let him sleep.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: He can sleep in my car while we wait. I said today; I'll hand you the lead before midnight.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get us to the wedding. Keep the hall key away from that cup of tea; the address is on the invitation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The key fell in. I used the invitation to dry it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll clean the key. You read out the address before the paper tears.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The address has washed off. The paper's stuck to the key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Empty the cup and put the key in it. I'll ring the couple for the address.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll seat everyone. Why is the cake on the last spare chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The table wobbles. I put the last guest on the piano stool.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll give the pianist my chair. You can move the cake to the table while I fix the leg.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake will fall if I put it there before you've fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hand it to me, then. You fix the leg; I'm standing anyway now the pianist has my chair.
